The family-owned and woman-owned company has built its reputation on quality, transparency, and deep expertise in detailing. Its team includes experienced detailers who understand the products firsthand, helping The Rag Company serve professionals and enthusiasts with premium microfiber towels, detailing accessories, chemicals, tools, and educational content.
That expertise has made The Rag Company more than a place to buy detailing products. It has become a trusted resource for people who care about getting better results from every detail.

The Rag Company had already built a respected brand and a catalog of more than 500 products. The next opportunity was making sure its Amazon listings reflected the same level of expertise and attention to detail that customers associated with its products.

The team wanted listing decisions to be grounded in evidence. Instead of simply rewriting product copy, they wanted to understand whether the search and advertising data they had accumulated could be translated into measurable gains in sales and key performance indicators.

There was also an important customer-experience opportunity. Product detail pages needed to answer the questions shoppers actually cared about, bring the most important features forward, and make it easier to understand why a product was the right choice.

For a brand with The Rag Company’s scale and category expertise, listing optimization needed to go beyond adding keywords or polishing copy. The team needed an approach that could complement its knowledge of detailing with data showing how Amazon shoppers actually searched, evaluated products, and purchased.
That made Quartile’s data-led approach a natural fit.

Rather than separating advertising insights from organic optimization, Quartile could use signals from both to identify the language and product attributes already connecting with customers. That gave The Rag Company a more informed way to improve its listings while preserving the product knowledge and credibility it had spent decades building.

Just as importantly, the pilot gave the team a way to validate the approach before expanding it. With more than 500 ASINs in the catalog, proving impact on high-priority products first created a disciplined path to scale.
Quartile and The Rag Company started where the potential impact was greatest: the brand’s best-selling products.

For its Gauntlet Car Drying Towel line, Quartile analyzed paid advertising and organic traffic data to understand the searches already bringing shoppers to the product and the terms associated with purchase behavior. Those insights became the foundation for optimizing the title, bullet points, and backend keywords.

Quartile reorganized the product’s bullet points so shoppers encountered the most relevant features first. The copy was designed to answer important customer questions more directly and make the product easier to evaluate as shoppers moved through the detail page.

The listing also reinforced an advantage The Rag Company had already earned: confidence in the brand. A dedicated bullet emphasized product quality and reliable performance, helping translate the company’s established reputation in the detailing community into a clearer Amazon shopping experience.
The result was not a listing written around search terms for their own sake. It was a listing informed by how real customers were already finding, evaluating, and buying the product.

This is the second installment of the "Statistics Basics" series. The only prerequisite is the median, which was covered in the first installment. The median was the middle value when data is arranged in ascending order (or the average of the two middle values if there is an even number of data points).
Quartiles are the "boundaries that divide data into four parts when arranged in ascending order"

Quartiles are the three boundaries that divide data arranged in ascending order into four groups of roughly equal size. Starting from the smallest, they are called the first quartile, second quartile, and third quartile.
